author: felicepantaleo
body:
`HGCalShowerShapeHelper::ShowerShapeCalc::getCellSize` gives the high-density cell size (`kHDWaferCellSize_` = 0.465 cm) only when `getSiThickIndex` returns 0, and the low-density cell size (`kLDWaferCellSize_` = 0.698 cm) otherwise. `getSiThickIndex` returns the silicon wafer type. Geometry v19 adds the type `HGCalHD200 = 3`, a high-density wafer with 200 um silicon. So the cells of `HGCalHD200` wafers get the low-density cell size.

This PR gives the high-density cell size to the two high-density types (`HGCalHD120`, `HGCalHD200`) and the low-density cell size to all other ids. HFNose and non-silicon ids keep the old result. A new Catch2 unit test checks each wafer type. Before the fix it fails for `HGCalHD200` (0.698 instead of 0.465).

`getRvar` widens its cylinder by the cell size of each hit. `getRvar` is an input of:

- the HGCAL supercluster regression of `particleFlowSuperClusterHGCal` (`SCEnergyCorrectorSemiParm::getRegDataHGCALV1`, input 14), which runs in the default Phase-2 reconstruction (`useRegression = True`, `isPhaseII = True` under `phase2_hgcal`);
- the HLT variable `hltEgammaHGCALIDVars*:rVar`. No HLT filter reads it.

The same pattern (type 0 is the only high-density type) is fixed in `HGCalDDDConstants`.

@bsunanda @pfs could you please check this? Does it need a backport to 20_0_X?
title: HGCAL v19: give the high-density cell values to HGCalHD200 in HGCalDDDConstants and HGCalShowerShapeHelper
